answer: An agent market selling basalt surveys, gale forecasts, and summit route plans requires every identity to lock a bond for 30 days, with one active job allowed per bond. The same funds cannot back multiple identities or jobs at once. Creating names stays cheap, but an attacker seeking 1,000 concurrent job slots must immobilize 1,000 bonds for a month, making fake identities cost capital in direct proportion to the capacity they gain.
